question:
Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}k & 2\\3 & k-1\end{bmatrix}$ and suppose that $|A|=-6$.

(a) Determine all possible real values of $k$.

(b) Find $A^{-1}$ corresponding to each value of $k$.

(c) Verify that both matrices obtained for $A$ are invertible.
explanation:
(a)
$$|A|=k(k-1)-6$$
Given that $|A|=-6$,
$$k(k-1)-6=-6$$
$$k(k-1)=0$$
Therefore,
$$k=0\quad\text{or}\quad k=1$$

(b)
For a matrix $\begin{bmatrix}a & b\\c & d\end{bmatrix}$, its inverse is
$$\frac{1}{ad-bc}\begin{bmatrix}d & -b\\-c & a\end{bmatrix}$$
For $k=0$,
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 2\\3 & -1\end{bmatrix}$$
Therefore,
$$A^{-1}=-\frac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix}-1 & -2\\-3 & 0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{6} & \frac{1}{3}\\\frac{1}{2} & 0\end{bmatrix}$$
For $k=1$,
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\3 & 0\end{bmatrix}$$
Therefore,
$$A^{-1}=-\frac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix}0 & -2\\-3 & 1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0 & \frac{1}{3}\\\frac{1}{2} & -\frac{1}{6}\end{bmatrix}$$

(c)
For both $k=0$ and $k=1$,
$$|A|=-6\neq0$$
Therefore, both corresponding matrices are invertible.

options.A:
(a) $k=-1$ or $k=2$
(b) For $k=-1$, $A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}\frac13&\frac13\\\frac12&\frac16\end{bmatrix}$; for $k=2$, $A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}-\frac16&\frac13\\\frac12&-\frac13\end{bmatrix}$
(c) Both matrices are invertible
options.B:
(a) $k=0$ or $k=1$
(b) For $k=0$, $A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}\frac16&\frac13\\\frac12&0\end{bmatrix}$; for $k=1$, $A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}0&\frac13\\\frac12&-\frac16\end{bmatrix}$
(c) Both are invertible since $|A|=-6\neq0$
options.C:
(a) $k=0$ only
(b) $A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}\frac16&\frac13\\\frac12&0\end{bmatrix}$
(c) The matrix corresponding to $k=1$ is singular
options.D:
(a) $k=0$ or $k=1$
(b) The corresponding inverse matrices are the negatives of those in option B
(c) Both matrices are singular because $|A|=-6$
